Release triage: saeka 9.5 / 10.0 and @telora/mcp-products 0.22.181

Judgment: BENIGN for each inspected archive. This means no demonstrated
malware behavior; Saeka remains an abuse-relevant card-checking utility.

Both Saeka archives have 12 regular files. Their chk.py bytes are identical
(SHA256 49c32bea3111e42fb3914086a0176926c4e1177d43040a65f8a03c44dad84a3e).
setup.py only declares setuptools metadata and the saeka console entrypoint.
The empty __init__.py does not trigger the checker. chk.py imports/install-falls
back to requests, colorama and cfonts, configures local storage, and hashes four
Base64-decoded hardcoded passwords for an interactive access gate. No decoded
payload executes. main() prompts for a menu; single/bulk/replay input comes
from operator input or chosen files. Full card tuples are posted to the
uncoder.eu.org checker; BIN prefixes go to binlist.net. Optional Tap/generic
checkout drivers post user-supplied card data using the configured API key or
checkout URL. Bulk processing rotates proxies and writes live results locally.
There is no hidden host-credential acquisition, backdoor, persistence, or
unrelated install-time payload. A malware-list entry alone cannot supply one.

Telora contains 162 regular source/declaration/source-map/package/doc files.
The MCP server exposes advertised product operations through validated schemas.
loadCredentials() reads TELORA_URL and TELORA_TRACKER_ID/TELORA_ACCESS_TOKEN or
its own .telora/daemon.json; callProductApi sends the configured token as Bearer
authorization to the configured product-api service. postinstall resolves two
installed Telora hook executables with which, exits if either is absent, and
merges PostToolUse/UserPromptSubmit command hooks into .claude/settings.json.
It does not download or execute connect.sh. That pipeline is a displayed setup
instruction, although following references correctly fetches it for analysis.
Requested connector/product operations can install and start the Telora daemon;
config, PID, signal, detached-spawn and log handling implement that function.
Initial and final followed scans also analyze the fetched dependency/reference
chain; it emits no suspicious or hostile traits. No payload was executed during
inspection. Native disassembly is inapplicable to these source-only archives;
binwalk is not installed in this environment.

Detection changes, by supported claim:
- Payment field names/filter fragments and their request-syntax co-occurrence
  move from credential-access to data/parse/payment, with neutral criticality.
  The old unused carveouts composite is retired; its loose OR never established
  a card-handling claim. The field-exclusion filter remains a neutral composite.
  PHP mail phishing still requires captured POST secrets and card-info mail;
  its exact card-field reference follows the move. The hostile PHP control
  verifies that attack coverage remains.
- Dot-name filters move from archive creation to fs/search. Their archive
  suppressor retains the exact same two predicates and exception scope, without
  claiming that either predicate proves archive creation. Ancestor selectors
  that positively need archives retain only archive-creation operations.
- Python os.listdir/os.scandir moves from drive enumeration to directory readdir;
  exact consumers follow. Existing readdir/glob observations are retained.
- /storage/emulated moves from disk wiping to personal/shared-storage paths;
  the original Android-wipe consumer retains its exact path-reference leg.
- getpass import moves to metadata/import/builtin, and getpass.getpass moves to
  ui/dialog/prompt; neither establishes current-user discovery. References
  retain their original import/prompt roles with no blanket package exclusions.
- Bare prompt(string) moves from browser forms to UI prompts, since local CLI
  helpers use that same signature. Its phishing consumer follows the exact move.
- execSync and exec/execSync ESM import atoms move to metadata/import/builtin;
  imports do not establish process creation. Python sys.executable/-m vector
  syntax moves to process/argument/option, without claiming a launch or cmd.exe.
- The cmd-specific spawn atom is consolidated into the existing variable-program
  spawn observation. The one npx-replacement consumer still requires explicit
  versioned-npx command construction plus a nearby variable-program spawn;
  renaming its local variable no longer disables that detection.
- Generic params.port no longer proves HTTP input. The request-port matcher
  requires POST/REQUEST or req.body/request.form. The positive HTTP control
  retains the destination composite; ordinary MCP params is the near miss.
- defaults read must have command-boundary spelling; comments saying
  org-defaults read no longer describe macOS command execution.
- Critical/required update prose moves to UI prompt text and requires an adjacent
  update message in a literal; schema words spread across text do not prove a
  fake-update lure. Its existing objective consumer follows the exact reference.
- which code must begin the command literal, so a documentation string ending
  in the words 'which code ' does not imply probing for a VS Code executable.
- The new card-tuple observation requires an actual regex-compilation call with
  a PAN/pipe/security-code regex argument, not a package name or fixed endpoint.
- The new UserPromptSubmit observation requires a parsed member access, matching
  the agent-hook namespace while excluding comment-only examples.

Positive and near-miss controls are listed in cases.json. They are exercised
with cleave --traits-dir . test-rules, including hostile phishing preservation.
Archive names, exact release numbers, sizes, reputation and ML scores do not
supply malicious traits or allowlist exceptions. Independent ML probabilities
remain elevated after YAML corrections and are not changed by this work.
